text.p: These are the leading stories in Sarajevo press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.

- Fulfilling the terms of the Dayton peace agreement is not a matter for compromise and comments by the deputy High Representative to Bosnia about the necessity of compromise encourages seccesionist forces obstructing the implementation of the treaty, says Kasim Begic, former advisor to Alija Izetbegovic, chairman of Bosnia's collective presidency.

- Orthodox Christian Bishop Vasilije Kacavenda cancelled trip to the town of Tuzla for Orthodox Easter celebrations after Moslem authorities in Tuzla fail to guarantee his safety because of his role in the Bosnian war.

- Some leaders spoiled Orthodox Easter in Tuzla by barring Kacavenda, said Michael Steiner, deputy High Representative. "I've spoken to people, including Srebrenica refugees, and they told me they did not mind if Kacavenda came," he said.
- Bosnian and U.S. doctors plan to perform heart surgery on a three-month old baby on Monday which is the first operation of its kind in the history of Bosnian medicine.
- The United States supports Bosnian opposition shadow government and promises concrete help, says opposition leader Sejfudin Tokic after a visit to Washington.
- A group of South Korean businessmen, inluding Samsung representatives, plan to visit Sarajevo soon to discuss investments in reconstruction projects.

- National bank governor Kasim Omicevic says that Bosnia's foreign debt is less then $2 billion and denies reports from the World Bank which put the debt at about $3.2 billion. -- Sarajevo newsroom +387-71-663-86
